name: Easton
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Easton, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Easton, MA: the Lions Holiday Festival and Reindog Parade, the Festival of Trees, Grinch fun at the Children's Museum and Santa.
lede: Easton does Christmas in North Easton village: the Lions Club fills the Rockery and Oakes Ames Memorial Hall with a two day festival and parade, and the Easton Charitable Trust decorates a whole Festival of Trees.
celebrates: The biggest weekend belongs to the Easton Lions Club Holiday Festival, held around the Rockery and Oakes Ames Memorial Hall in North Easton. It brings a crafts marketplace inside the hall, free music on the Rockery, visits with Santa and a holiday parade down Main Street that includes the Gus Arns Memorial Reindog Parade, where dogs march in costume. The Easton Charitable Trust runs the Festival of Trees, its largest fundraiser, which the trust says has returned nearly $500,000 to local nonprofits. The Children's Museum in Easton, whose exhibits are designed for ages 1 to 7, adds holiday programs of its own.
lastyear: In 2025 the 40th Easton Lions Holiday Festival ran December 6 and 7 at Oakes Ames Memorial Hall and the Natural Resources Trust of Easton at 307 Main Street. The Enterprise listed an inflatable slide, bouncy houses, a trackless train, hayrides, a climbing wall, s'mores at firepits, a Scout breakfast, kids crafts and a carnival. Saturday ended with the lighting of the Rockery, and the Reindog Parade entry fee was cans of pet food for the Animal Protection Center. The Festival of Trees distributed $65,000 that year.
facts: The Easton Lions Holiday Festival began in 1986 at the Rockery and Oakes Ames Memorial Hall, and the Lions took it over in 1988 from the Easton Businessman's Association. The Rockery was restored to its 1882 appearance in the mid 2000s, and in 2020 the Avery Lee Williams Family Trust donated the Santa's House where children now meet Santa. North Easton is also home to five buildings by the architect Henry Hobson Richardson.
trains: Trains are part of North Easton's history. Henry Hobson Richardson designed the Old Colony Railroad Station in 1881 for a line that reached North Easton from Stoughton in 1855. Trains had stopped running for more than ten years when members of the Ames family bought the station in 1969 and gave it to the Easton Historical Society, which still uses it. Today the closest MBTA Commuter Rail stop is Stoughton station, the end of the Stoughton Branch of the Providence/Stoughton Line.

kidfact: Easton's old train station was designed in 1881 by a famous architect named Henry Hobson Richardson. The trains stopped coming long ago, and now the station is a history museum.
faq: What is the Easton Lions Holiday Festival?

It is a two day holiday festival run by the Easton Lions Club around the Rockery and Oakes Ames Memorial Hall in North Easton. It started in 1986, and the Lions took it over in 1988. Families find rides, crafts, a marketplace, music, visits with Santa, a parade on Main Street and the lighting of the Rockery.
What is the Reindog Parade in Easton?

The Gus Arns Memorial Reindog Parade is part of the Easton Lions Holiday Festival parade. Dogs dress up for the holidays and march along Main Street toward the Rockery after a judging. In 2025 the entry fee was one or more cans of pet food, donated to the Animal Protection Center.
What is the Easton Festival of Trees?

It is the Easton Charitable Trust's largest fundraiser of the year, a display of decorated trees with raffles at Easton Country Club in South Easton. The trust says the festival has returned nearly $500,000 to local nonprofits over the years, including $65,000 distributed in 2025.
Where is Santa's House in Easton?

Santa's House stands at the Rockery in North Easton during the Easton Lions Holiday Festival. The Avery Lee Williams Family Trust donated it to the festival in 2020. Children visit Santa there during the festival weekend, and the Lions schedule lists set times for the visits each day.
Does Easton have a train station?

Easton has no MBTA stop today. The historic Old Colony Railroad Station in North Easton, designed by H. H. Richardson in 1881, now houses the Easton Historical Society. The nearest Commuter Rail stop is Stoughton station, at the end of the Stoughton Branch of the Providence/Stoughton Line.
